facts.text: Baker was named after Milwaukee Road engineer A.G. Baker, who helped build the rail line that brought the town to life.
The O’Fallon Historical Museum in Baker proudly houses the world’s largest steer, a quirky reminder of the town’s ranching past.
Every June, Baker hosts Heritage Fest at the O’Fallon Historical Museum, where locals celebrate history with hands‑on traditions and storytelling.
Baker’s origins trace back to a lake the Milwaukee Road created to supply water to its steam locomotives, a key stop on the transcontinental line.
Baker’s radio scene features two stations: KFLN AM, a country music outlet, and KJJM FM, which plays classic rock for the community.
